subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: What cancellation or provider-safe fencing contract should govern OAuth refreshes once the held-lock deadline expires, so a successor cannot race a still-running token refresh?
rationale: The branch correctly protects local writes after abandonment, but the remaining side effect is at the OAuth provider and cannot be settled from local state guards alone.

options.title: Require cancellation or fencing before unlock
options.body: Redesign the deadline path so a potentially token-rotating request cannot overlap a successor refresh, then prove the concurrent-refresh outcome.

options.title: Accept the provider-side race
options.body: Land the current local write protections while explicitly accepting that an abandoned remote refresh may disrupt a successor credential refresh.

options.title: Pause the deadline expansion
options.body: Keep the existing lock serialization until a provider-compatible cancellation or recovery design is available.

recommendation.title: Require cancellation or fencing before unlock
recommendation.body: Redesign the deadline path so a potentially token-rotating request cannot overlap a successor refresh, then prove the concurrent-refresh outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the OAuth refresh failure and provider/profile handling path most directly implicated by the remaining race.
